subject: Trial alignment: scope, success gates, and eval method
messages:

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Trial alignment: scope, success gates, and eval method
Attachments: Symphony_trial_charter_v0.1.pdf (application/pdf), shadow_vs_offline_matters.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Hi Claire / Roberto — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Call summary (high level)
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for structured Q&A and content normalization across a subset of Symphony’s provider-content workflows.
- Desired outcome: measurable decrease in manual review volume (target: 30% reduction) and pass-rate ≥ 90% on accuracy rubric for canonical mappings.

Proposed trial scope & cadence
1) Data prep (2 weeks): Symphony shares sample dataset + redaction guidance; Redwood provides ingestion checklist and example prompts.
2) Evaluation phase (4 weeks): run a combined approach: either A) 2-week offline automated eval followed by 2-week online shadow, or B) 4-week shadow-only. We asked whether you prefer offline-first vs shadow-first — see question below.
3) Success gates: automated precision ≥ 0.88 OR human-reviewed pass-rate ≥ 0.90; latency p95 < 600ms for average request size; no critical security issues in logging/pII handling.

Ownership
- Symphony: Claire (product lead) + Roberto (data ops) — data access, schema mapping, accept/reject labels.
- Redwood: Soojin (trial ops owner), Marissa (eval design / scoring), Vivek (infra & config).

Open questions / asks for Symphony
- Which evaluation order do you prefer (offline-first to sanity-check metrics, then shadow), or start with shadow to validate end-to-end behavior?
- Please confirm team members for security & SRE so we can share network/PII controls.
- Share an initial 500–1,000 sample records for a dry run.

Next steps (recommended)
- You confirm the evaluation order and provide security contact by EOD Wednesday (Aug 11).
- Redwood: we push trial charter + evaluation rubric (attached) and a kickoff invite for Aug 16 if that works.

Attachments: trial charter (high level), decision matrix on shadow vs offline (short pros/cons).

Thanks — appreciate the clear priorities on your side. I’ll update the HubSpot record after we confirm.

Best,
Soojin

Thanks, Soojin — great summary. Short answers below and a couple of asks from our side.

We’d prefer option A: start with a 2-week offline automated eval to validate metrics without impacting production flows, then move to a 2-week shadow run. Doing offline-first helps us tune thresholds and reduces ops churn.

Security ask: can you share what level of logging Redwood will capture for shadow runs (full payload, redacted fields, or only metadata)? We need to validate against our privacy policy. Please loop our security contact (security@symphonyhealth.ai) on the next communication.

Sample data: we can provide an initial set of 750 de-identified records by Tue Aug 10 EOD.

Confirming owners here — I’ll escalate to our SRE/security if you need additional signoffs. Kickoff Aug 16 works for us.

Hi all — thanks for the clear direction. I’ve attached a proposed evaluation rubric (spreadsheet) and include a short summary below so the scoring is explicit for both offline and shadow runs.

Summary of proposed rubric & weighting (draft)
- Accuracy / canonical mapping precision: 40% (automated scoring vs ground-truth labels)
- Human review pass-rate (end-to-end): 30% (sampled manual grading during shadow)
- Hallucination / incorrect extractions: 15% (critical = immediate fail)
- Latency & reliability (p95): 10% (goal p95 < 600ms)
- Token cost / throughput efficiency: 5%

Pass thresholds (suggested)
- Automated precision >= 0.88 AND human pass-rate >= 0.90 to consider feature ‘go’ for expanded traffic.
- If automated precision is 0.82–0.88, require shadow + manual review for 30% of requests until precision improves.

Offline vs Shadow: operational notes
- Offline automated eval: we run the sample through the same inference configuration we’ll use in shadow. We compute precision/recall, false-positive examples, and representative error cases.
- Shadow run: requests mirror production routing; Symphony reviewers will see both Redwood output and original source; reviewers will mark accept/reject and flag hallucinations. We’ll supply a UI/CSV for quick grading.

Proposal: start offline for 2 weeks to baseline precision, then a 2-week shadow to validate end-to-end UX. During the offline run we’ll surface the top 20 failure cases for collaborative review.

Operational asks from Redwood
- Provide sample records + label format by Tue Aug 10 EOD.
- Point person for test environment network IP allowlist; Vivek will send a minimal config.

I’ll schedule a 30-min dry-run session where we run 100 sample records through the pipeline and review the rubric results together. If everyone agrees, I’ll send calendar invites after Claire confirms security contact.

Thanks — happy to iterate on weights if you have domain-specific priorities (e.g., prefer recall over precision).

Marissa Cole
Principal ML Product Manager | Redwood Inference
